ai.title: Replace inf wrapper with .bin/bun binstub and direnv for secrets
ai.summary: Removed the manual `inf` wrapper script and `bun run inf` calls in favor of a local `.bin/bun` binstub that selectively injects Infisical secrets. The new wrapper detects commands like `test`, `dev`, `start`, or scripts matching secret-dependent patterns (e.g., `db:*`) and executes `infisical run` before the real Bun binary, while passing through others directly. Updated `backend`, `common`, `evals`, and `npm-app` package.json scripts to call `bun` directly, relying on `direnv` (via `.envrc.example`) to prepend `.bin` to the PATH. Documentation in `README.md` and `direnv-test-plan.md` details the new setup requiring `direnv` installation and `direnv allow`.

eli5.text: When you run common project commands like tests or your local server, the system now automatically loads your secure login credentials for databases and other services behind the scenes, instead of requiring you to manually trigger a separate setup step each time. The old approach asked you to run a special helper script before every command; the new approach quietly checks whether the command you typed needs those credentials and, if so, fetches them automatically. If you look at how things are wired together, you'll see that the list of commands needing credentials is now defined inside a single launcher that replaces the old helper, and the project's setup instructions have been rewritten to tell you to install one additional tool and grant it permission. ai.title: Remove direnv-test-plan.md
ai.summary: Deleted direnv-test-plan.md. File contained internal notes on selective bun binstub wrapping for Infisical secret injection via direnv. Repo-only cleanup. No code or config changes.

eli5.text: The team deleted an old planning document that laid out a step-by-step approach for automatically supplying secure access credentials to development tools only when a specific task actually needed them, so routine tasks like installing packages would run faster and with fewer exposed secrets. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping and has no effect on any product behavior you would see. If you opened the code repository today, you would notice that the old planning note is gone, and nothing else changes.

ai.title: Remove infisical wrapper from unit test hooks
ai.summary: Removed `infisical run --` prefix from `backend-unit-tests`, `npm-app-unit-tests`, and `common-unit-tests` commands in `codebuff.json`. Unit tests now execute `bun test` directly without the secrets manager wrapper. This change applies to all three file change hooks defined in the repo configuration.

eli5.text: The automated tests that run when code changes are saved no longer route through the organization's secrets manager. If you looked at the configuration, you would see the test commands call the test runner directly instead of wrapping them in a secrets-fetching tool, and the same simplification appears across all three test hooks in the internal repo config.
